text:
maria: Heads up — since the calico upgrade off-hours (v3.28.x -> v3.29.x) we're seeing a spike in pod -> pod packet drops and long tail latency across eu-west1 GPU clusters. Noticed during model checkpoint syncs (RDMA-ish handshakes failing).

kevin: seeing the same for p2 and p3 node pools, +20% retransmits on perf tests. Logs show TCP resets during KV cache fetches between pods.

raj: tagged the networking tests. Any MTU changes in the calico config?

maria: we didn't touch MTU in our manifests, but the operator bumped dataplane to eBPF mode. Could be GSO/GRO interaction with NIC offloads.

tess: timeline — calico-operator CR applied at 02:13 UTC, rolling update finished by 03:02. First errors started ~03:15.

sre-bot: [ALERT] network-packetloss-high eu-west1-gpu: p50 latency 1.2s -> 2.9s, packet loss 7% over last 5m :warning:

kevin: quick probe: iperf3 pod->pod on same node is fine, cross-node shows bursts of drops. Could be east-west encapsulation fragmentation.

raj: can you dump iptables/nft rules and 'calico/node' kernel logs from a hit pair?

kevin: pastebin gist: https://gist.example/iperf-crossnode.txt — shows retransmit spikes during 64k bursts.

maria: grabbed dmesg from one problematic node: ``[calico] skb_frags: GSO fragment failed: -22`` repeated.

tess: that error smells like GSO split failing with Geneve/GRE overhead + MTU. But we're using IP-in-IP with eBPF encapsulation now.

raj: check PMTU between nodes:
```
# on node-a
ip route get 10.32.5.12
ping -M do -s 1472 10.32.5.12
```

kevin: ping with do-not-fragment fails at 1400, we had been using 1450 previously. Something changed during upgrade (maybe iptables conntrack expectations).

maria: also seeing RDMA connect timeouts in logs for TF allreduce jobs: "rdma: timeout waiting for cm_event" — often requires in-order packet delivery, sensitive to fragmentation.

tess: immediate mitigation options: 1) rollback calico to previous release; 2) force IPIP->VXLAN switch (but VXLAN might also interact); 3) set host MTU lower via DaemonSet to avoid fragmentation.

raj: rolling back is fastest. Any constraints? Dedicated customers on eu-west1 might be affected by brief restart of calico pods.

maria: impact: ongoing training jobs see >3x step latency tails; ops says 8 VIP customers in affected AZs. Recommend controlled rollback to v3.28.4 and keep canary on a few nodes.

deploy-bot: calico-operator rollout started: namespace=calico-system, target_version=3.28.4, rollout_id=rl-213333. will undo daemonset updates.

kevin: after rollback started — watch for flapping. I'll instrument packet capture between two GPU pods during rollback: `tcpdump -i any -w /tmp/capture.pcap host 10.32.5.12 and host 10.32.6.13`

maria: Also adding temporary iptables rule to drop GRO/GSO coalesced large segments? Not ideal but can reduce fragment failures: `ethtool -K eth0 gso off gro off tso off` (applied via DaemonSet for the node).

tess: ops concern: ethtool toggles will hit CPU cost — might increase host CPU usage during GPU jobs. Use as last resort for small window.

sre-bot: [INFO] rollback in progress; monitoring packetloss and RDMA connect success rate.

raj: post-rollback checks: p50/p95/p99 latencies trending down, packet loss back to <1% on initial probes. Please keep canary nodes in eu-west1-b for 2 hours to validate.

kevin: captured pcaps show GSO fragments vanish after rollback; RDMA handshakes successful again.

maria: follow-up: open incident ticket INF-2026-421, note root cause suspected: calico eBPF dataplane + NIC offload interaction causing GSO split failures leading to fragmentation/packet loss on high-throughput east-west flows (RDMA-sensitive).

tess: actions: 1) keep rollback, 2) run MTU/GSO test matrix against calico v3.29 in staging with identical NIC drivers, 3) coordinate with calico upstream for a fix or suggested kernel flags, 4) add canary gating to operator upgrades for GPU node pools.

raj: tagging kernel/driver team and customer-success for outreach.

maria: thanks all — leaving alert on until we confirm no regressions after 2h. :thumbsup:
